WT-2026-07 — Boundary Layer Wind Study, Building A2
Sawtooth Wind Engineering · final report · 22 July 2026 · 1:200 scale rigid model, suburban-to-open rural approach, Exposure C target profile
1. Scope
A pressure-model study of Building A2 in its as-built massing, including the generator-yard re-entrant corner and the
mechanical screen wall, to provide main wind force resisting system pressure coefficients for the roof diaphragm and
shear wall design.
2. Model and instrumentation
Rigid pressure model at 1:200, 512 surface taps on the four elevations and the two notch elevations, sampled at 512 Hz
for 180 s at each azimuth, 36 azimuths at 10 degree increments. Results are reported at the eight cardinal and
intercardinal azimuths, which envelope the measured set for every wall line.
3. Reference pressure
Every coefficient in this report and in the accompanying data file is referenced to the velocity pressure at mean
roof height, q_h. The height variation of the windward pressure is contained in the reported coefficients; the design
pressure on a wall patch is p = q_h * Cp and no further height adjustment is to be applied.
4. Azimuth convention
An azimuth is the direction the wind comes FROM, measured clockwise from north: 0 degrees is a wind from the north
blowing toward the south, 90 degrees is a wind from the east.
5. Patch convention
The facade is divided into patches. A patch covers the full length of one precast panel and one elevation band. The
bands are B1 = 0 to 7 ft, B2 = 7 to 14 ft, B3 = 14 to 21 ft, B4 = 21 to 28 ft, and the band identified P is the parapet - the
strip from the roof deck to the top of that panel, whatever its height. A patch identifier is the panel mark followed by
the band: S06-B3 is panel S06 between 14 and 21 ft, N108-P is the parapet strip of panel N108. Panel lengths and
top elevations are not reproduced here; they are properties of the as-built model.
6. Coefficients
6.1 Wall patches. The data file gives the mean pressure coefficient Cp for each wall patch and azimuth. Positive is
toward the surface.
6.2 The re-entrant corner of the generator yard produces a locally amplified suction on the two notch elevations at every
azimuth; that amplification is in the reported coefficients.
6.3 Parapet patches. For a parapet the data file gives the NET coefficient GCpn, which acts on the parapet's projected
area and already accounts for both faces: +1.5 on a windward parapet and -1.0 on a leeward parapet, interpolated on
the cosine of the incidence for an oblique wind. The net parapet pressure is p = q_p * GCpn with q_p the velocity
pressure at the top of that parapet, not at mean roof height - the screen wall on the north elevation reaches well
above the deck and its velocity pressure is correspondingly higher.
6.4 Internal pressure is not part of this study.
7. Data file
WT-2026-07_Cp_by_azimuth.csv, columns patch_id, azimuth_deg, cp. One row per patch per azimuth.
8. Uncertainty

--- Page 2 ---
WT-2026-07 Boundary Layer Wind Study
page 2
The tap-to-tap repeatability of the reported means is +/- 0.03 in Cp. The coefficients are reported to four decimal places
for traceability, not because they are known to that precision.
9. Limitations
The study covers the as-built massing of 2026. It does not cover the roof-mounted equipment, the screen wall's own
component-and-cladding pressures, or any future Building A3 to the east.

(a) General. (1) Except as provided in paragraph (a)(2) of this section, where steel joists are used and columns are not framed in at least two directions with solid web structural steel members, a steel joist shall be field-bolted at the column to provide lateral stability to the column during erection. For the installation of this joist:

(i) A vertical stabilizer plate shall be provided on each column for steel joists. The plate shall be a minimum of 6 inch by 6 inch (152 mm by 152 mm) and shall extend at least 3 inches (76 mm) below the bottom chord of the joist with a 13/16 inch (21 mm) hole to provide an attachment point for guying or plumbing cables.

(ii) The bottom chords of steel joists at columns shall be stabilized to prevent rotation during erection.

(iii) Hoisting cables shall not be released until the seat at each end of the steel joist is field-bolted, and each end of the bottom chord is restrained by the column stabilizer plate.

(2) Where constructibility does not allow a steel joist to be installed at the column:

(i) an alternate means of stabilizing joists shall be installed on both sides near the column and shall:

(A) provide stability equivalent to paragraph (a)(1) of this section;

(B) be designed by a qualified person;

(C) be shop installed; and

(D) be included in the erection drawings.

(ii) hoisting cables shall not be released until the seat at each end of the steel joist is field-bolted and the joist is stabilized.

(3) Where steel joists at or near columns span 60 feet (18.3 m) or less, the joist shall be designed with sufficient strength to allow one employee to release the hoisting cable without the need for erection bridging.

(4) Where steel joists at or near columns span more than 60 feet (18.3 m), the joists shall be set in tandem with all bridging installed unless an alternative method of erection, which provides equivalent stability to the steel joist, is designed by a qualified person and is included in the site-specific erection plan.

(5) A steel joist or steel joist girder shall not be placed on any support structure unless such structure is stabilized.

(6) When steel joist(s) are landed on a structure, they shall be secured to prevent unintentional displacement prior to installation.

(7) No modification that affects the strength of a steel joist or steel joist girder shall be made without the approval of the project structural engineer of record.

(8) Field-bolted joists. (i) Except for steel joists that have been pre-assembled into panels, connections of individual steel joists to steel structures in bays of 40 feet (12.2 m) or more shall be fabricated to allow for field bolting during erection.

(ii) These connections shall be field-bolted unless constructibility does not allow.

(9) Steel joists and steel joist girders shall not be used as anchorage points for a fall arrest system unless written approval to do so is obtained from a qualified person.

(10) A bridging terminus point shall be established before bridging is installed. (See appendix C to this subpart.)

(b) Attachment of steel joists and steel joist girders. (1) Each end of “K” series steel joists shall be attached to the support structure with a minimum of two 1/8-inch (3 mm) fillet welds 1 inch (25 mm) long or with two 1/2-inch (13 mm) bolts, or the equivalent.

(2) Each end of “LH” and “DLH” series steel joists and steel joist girders shall be attached to the support structure with a minimum of two 1/4-inch (6 mm) fillet welds 2 inches (51 mm) long, or with two 3/4-inch (19 mm) bolts, or the equivalent.

(3) Except as provided in paragraph (b)(4) of this section, each steel joist shall be attached to the support structure, at least at one end on both sides of the seat, immediately upon placement in the final erection position and before additional joists are placed.

(4) Panels that have been pre-assembled from steel joists with bridging shall be attached to the structure at each corner before the hoisting cables are released.

(c) Erection of steel joists. (1) Both sides of the seat of one end of each steel joist that requires bridging under Tables A and B shall be attached to the support structure before hoisting cables are released.

(2) For joists over 60 feet, both ends of the joist shall be attached as specified in paragraph (b) of this section and the provisions of paragraph (d) of this section met before the hoisting cables are released.

(3) On steel joists that do not require erection bridging under Tables A and B, only one employee shall be allowed on the joist until all bridging is installed and anchored.

[TABLE OMITTED]
[TABLE OMITTED]

(4) Employees shall not be allowed on steel joists where the span of the steel joist is equal to or greater than the span shown in Tables A and B except in accordance with § 1926.757(d).

(5) When permanent bridging terminus points cannot be used during erection, additional temporary bridging terminus points are required to provide stability. (See appendix C of this subpart.)

(d) Erection bridging. (1) Where the span of the steel joist is equal to or greater than the span shown in Tables A and B, the following shall apply:

(i) A row of bolted diagonal erection bridging shall be installed near the midspan of the steel joist;

(ii) Hoisting cables shall not be released until this bolted diagonal erection bridging is installed and anchored; and

(iii) No more than one employee shall be allowed on these spans until all other bridging is installed and anchored.

(2) Where the span of the steel joist is over 60 feet (18.3 m) through 100 feet (30.5 m), the following shall apply:

(i) All rows of bridging shall be bolted diagonal bridging;

(ii) Two rows of bolted diagonal erection bridging shall be installed near the third points of the steel joist;

(iii) Hoisting cables shall not be released until this bolted diagonal erection bridging is installed and anchored; and

(iv) No more than two employees shall be allowed on these spans until all other bridging is installed and anchored.

(3) Where the span of the steel joist is over 100 feet (30.5 m) through 144 feet (43.9 m), the following shall apply:

(i) All rows of bridging shall be bolted diagonal bridging;

(ii) Hoisting cables shall not be released until all bridging is installed and anchored; and

(iii) No more than two employees shall be allowed on these spans until all bridging is installed and anchored.

(4) For steel members spanning over 144 feet (43.9 m), the erection methods used shall be in accordance with § 1926.756.

(5) Where any steel joist specified in paragraphs (c)(2) and (d)(1), (d)(2), and (d)(3) of this section is a bottom chord bearing joist, a row of bolted diagonal bridging shall be provided near the support(s). This bridging shall be installed and anchored before the hoisting cable(s) is released.

(6) When bolted diagonal erection bridging is required by this section, the following shall apply:

(i) The bridging shall be indicated on the erection drawing;

(ii) The erection drawing shall be the exclusive indicator of the proper placement of this bridging;

(iii) Shop-installed bridging clips, or functional equivalents, shall be used where the bridging bolts to the steel joists;

(iv) When two pieces of bridging are attached to the steel joist by a common bolt, the nut that secures the first piece of bridging shall not be removed from the bolt for the attachment of the second; and

(v) Bridging attachments shall not protrude above the top chord of the steel joist.

(e) Landing and placing loads. (1) During the construction period, the employer placing a load on steel joists shall ensure that the load is distributed so as not to exceed the carrying capacity of any steel joist.

(2) Except for paragraph (e)(4) of this section, no construction loads are allowed on the steel joists until all bridging is installed and anchored and all joist-bearing ends are attached.

(3) The weight of a bundle of joist bridging shall not exceed a total of 1,000 pounds (454 kg). A bundle of joist bridging shall be placed on a minimum of three steel joists that are secured at one end. The edge of the bridging bundle shall be positioned within 1 foot (.30 m) of the secured end.

(4) No bundle of decking may be placed on steel joists until all bridging has been installed and anchored and all joist bearing ends attached, unless all of the following conditions are met:

(i) The employer has first determined from a qualified person and documented in a site-specific erection plan that the structure or portion of the structure is capable of supporting the load;

(ii) The bundle of decking is placed on a minimum of three steel joists;

(iii) The joists supporting the bundle of decking are attached at both ends;

(iv) At least one row of bridging is installed and anchored;

(v) The total weight of the bundle of decking does not exceed 4,000 pounds (1816 kg); and

(vi) Placement of the bundle of decking shall be in accordance with paragraph (e)(5) of this section.

(5) The edge of the construction load shall be placed within 1 foot (.30 m) of the bearing surface of the joist end.

(i) All rows of bridging shall be bolted diagonal bridging;

(iii) Hoisting cables shall not be released until this bolted diagonal erection bridging is installed and anchored; and

(iv) No more than two employees shall be allowed on these spans until all other bridging is installed and anchored.

(ii) The bundle of decking is placed on a minimum of three steel joists;

(3) Where the span of the steel joist is over 100 feet (30.5 m) through 144 feet (43.9 m), the following shall apply:

(i) All rows of bridging shall be bolted diagonal bridging;

(ii) Hoisting cables shall not be released until all bridging is installed and anchored; and

(iii) No more than two employees shall be allowed on these spans until all bridging is installed and anchored.

(4) For steel members spanning over 144 feet (43.9 m), the erection methods used shall be in accordance with § 1926.756.

(5) Where any steel joist specified in paragraphs (c)(2) and (d)(1), (d)(2), and (d)(3) of this section is a bottom chord bearing joist, a row of bolted diagonal bridging shall be provided near the support(s). This bridging shall be installed and anchored before the hoisting cable(s) is released.

(6) When bolted diagonal erection bridging is required by this section, the following shall apply:

(i) The bridging shall be indicated on the erection drawing;

(ii) The erection drawing shall be the exclusive indicator of the proper placement of this bridging;

(iii) Shop-installed bridging clips, or functional equivalents, shall be used where the bridging bolts to the steel joists;

(iv) When two pieces of bridging are attached to the steel joist by a common bolt, the nut that secures the first piece of bridging shall not be removed from the bolt for the attachment of the second; and

(v) Bridging attachments shall not protrude above the top chord of the steel joist.

(e) Landing and placing loads. (1) During the construction period, the employer placing a load on steel joists shall ensure that the load is distributed so as not to exceed the carrying capacity of any steel joist.

(2) Except for paragraph (e)(4) of this section, no construction loads are allowed on the steel joists until all bridging is installed and anchored and all joist-bearing ends are attached.

(3) The weight of a bundle of joist bridging shall not exceed a total of 1,000 pounds (454 kg). A bundle of joist bridging shall be placed on a minimum of three steel joists that are secured at one end. The edge of the bridging bundle shall be positioned within 1 foot (.30 m) of the secured end.

(4) No bundle of decking may be placed on steel joists until all bridging has been installed and anchored and all joist bearing ends attached, unless all of the following conditions are met:

(i) The employer has first determined from a qualified person and documented in a site-specific erection plan that the structure or portion of the structure is capable of supporting the load;

(ii) The bundle of decking is placed on a minimum of three steel joists;

(iii) The joists supporting the bundle of decking are attached at both ends;

(iv) At least one row of bridging is installed and anchored;

(v) The total weight of the bundle of decking does not exceed 4,000 pounds (1816 kg); and

(vi) Placement of the bundle of decking shall be in accordance with paragraph (e)(5) of this section.

(5) The edge of the construction load shall be placed within 1 foot (.30 m) of the bearing surface of the joist end.

9. DIAPH-MT 1.0 - the required diaphragm analysis
The roof deck diaphragm is neither rigid nor flexible relative to the precast walls: the walls are stiff, the wall lines are not
collinear, and the re-entrant corner at the generator yard has no wall on two of its sides. A tributary (flexible) or a rigid
distribution is not accepted for this building. The following semi-rigid model is required, and the submitted

9.1 Mesh. A structured square mesh of side H is laid over the bounding rectangle of the roof, with its origin at the
building grid origin. A cell belongs to the diaphragm when its centre lies inside the roof outline and outside a roof
opening. Nodes are the corners of the cells that belong. Refinement levels: L1 H = 10.0 ft, L2 H = 5.0 ft, L3 H = 2.50 ft.
9.2 Elements. Each cell is a four-node bilinear membrane integrated with 2 x 2 Gauss quadrature, carrying the stress
resultants
    Nx  = EAx * eps_x        Ny = EAy * eps_y        Nxy = Ghat * gamma
    Ghat = 12 * G'           [kip/ft, with G' in kip/in]
EAx and EAy are the smeared axial rigidity of the roof framing, in kips per foot of width, computed as the chord area of
the member divided by its spacing times Es = 29,000 ksi - the girders east-west and the joists north-south, both from
the framing plan and the joist schedule. The deck itself is not credited with axial rigidity.
9.3 Chords and collectors are two-node bar elements of area A and Es = 29,000 ksi on the lines of section 10, one
bar per mesh interval, acting in the direction of the line.
9.4 Supports. Each pier of 5.5 is a spring of stiffness k acting in the plane of its wall, attached at the mesh node
nearest the mid-point of the leg. Where two piers resolve to the same node their stiffnesses add.
9.5 Loads. The roof-level line load of 6.4 is applied to the perimeter nodes of its wall line as the consistent nodal loads
of the piecewise-linear hat functions between adjacent nodes on that line.
9.6 Recovery. The diaphragm unit shear of an element is Ghat times the engineering shear strain at the element
centre. The unit shear reported at a station on a wall line is that of the element which has an edge on that wall line and
whose centre is nearest the station. A wall line's reaction is the sum of its piers' spring forces. A chord or collector force
is the largest bar force on that line.

L2 and L3 in the reaction of wall line W under scenario W01, which must not exceed 5 %. The largest unit shear in the
building is a corner quantity and does not converge at that rate; report it at each level, but do not use it as the

TS-2026-02 — Site-Specific Topographic Wind Study
Sawtooth Wind Engineering · 30 April 2026 · Northern Divide Data Campus, Building A2
1. Setting
The campus occupies a bench on the west side of the valley. The ground rises about 190 ft over roughly 1,500 ft from
the valley floor to the bench, and the parcel sits within the upper quarter of that rise.
2. Feature classification
The feature is an escarpment for winds from the east through south-east and a two-dimensional ridge for winds from
the west. The escarpment case governs.
3. Method
Speed-up was evaluated from the measured terrain profile along sixteen radials and checked against the model study's
approach flow.
4. Result
The topographic factor to be applied over the whole Building A2 footprint, at all elevations and for all azimuths,
is Kzt = 1.19. No reduction with height is taken within the height of this building.
5. Note on earlier work

WT-2026-07 — Boundary Layer Wind Study, Building A2
Sawtooth Wind Engineering · final report · 22 July 2026 · 1:200 scale rigid model, suburban-to-open rural approach, Exposure C target profile
1. Scope
A pressure-model study of Building A2 in its as-built massing, including the generator-yard re-entrant corner and the
mechanical screen wall, to provide main wind force resisting system pressure coefficients for the roof diaphragm and
shear wall design.
2. Model and instrumentation
Rigid pressure model at 1:200, 512 surface taps on the four elevations and the two notch elevations, sampled at 512 Hz
for 180 s at each azimuth, 36 azimuths at 10 degree increments. Results are reported at the eight cardinal and
intercardinal azimuths, which envelope the measured set for every wall line.
3. Reference pressure
Every coefficient in this report and in the accompanying data file is referenced to the velocity pressure at mean
roof height, q_h. The height variation of the windward pressure is contained in the reported coefficients; the design
pressure on a wall patch is p = q_h * Cp and no further height adjustment is to be applied.
4. Azimuth convention
An azimuth is the direction the wind comes FROM, measured clockwise from north: 0 degrees is a wind from the north
blowing toward the south, 90 degrees is a wind from the east.
5. Patch convention
The facade is divided into patches. A patch covers the full length of one precast panel and one elevation band. The
bands are B1 = 0 to 7 ft, B2 = 7 to 14 ft, B3 = 14 to 21 ft, B4 = 21 to 28 ft, and the band identified P is the parapet - the
strip from the roof deck to the top of that panel, whatever its height. A patch identifier is the panel mark followed by
the band: S06-B3 is panel S06 between 14 and 21 ft, N108-P is the parapet strip of panel N108. Panel lengths and
top elevations are not reproduced here; they are properties of the as-built model.
6. Coefficients
6.1 Wall patches. The data file gives the mean pressure coefficient Cp for each wall patch and azimuth. Positive is
toward the surface.
6.2 The re-entrant corner of the generator yard produces a locally amplified suction on the two notch elevations at every
azimuth; that amplification is in the reported coefficients.
6.3 Parapet patches. For a parapet the data file gives the NET coefficient GCpn, which acts on the parapet's projected
area and already accounts for both faces: +1.5 on a windward parapet and -1.0 on a leeward parapet, interpolated on
the cosine of the incidence for an oblique wind. The net parapet pressure is p = q_p * GCpn with q_p the velocity
pressure at the top of that parapet, not at mean roof height - the screen wall on the north elevation reaches well
above the deck and its velocity pressure is correspondingly higher.
6.4 Internal pressure is not part of this study.
7. Data file
WT-2026-07_Cp_by_azimuth.csv, columns patch_id, azimuth_deg, cp. One row per patch per azimuth.
8. Uncertainty

The tap-to-tap repeatability of the reported means is +/- 0.03 in Cp. The coefficients are reported to four decimal places
for traceability, not because they are known to that precision.
9. Limitations
The study covers the as-built massing of 2026. It does not cover the roof-mounted equipment, the screen wall's own
component-and-cladding pressures, or any future Building A3 to the east.

cells, nodes, node_map, bar_elems, pier_nodes, F_all, U_all = run_diaph_mt(5.0, zone_Gp, c_areas)

print("\n=== DRIFT (in) for D18-36/7-4 ===")
for s_idx, (sname, az, fac, ecc, B_dim) in enumerate(scenarios):
    u = U_all[:, s_idx]
    for axis, aname in [(0, "X"), (1, "Y")]:
        k_sum = sum(k_ft for p, n_idx, ax, k_ft in pier_nodes if ax == axis)
        u_mean = sum(k_ft * u[2*n_idx + axis] for p, n_idx, ax, k_ft in pier_nodes if ax == axis) / k_sum
        defl_in = np.max(np.abs(u[axis::2] - u_mean)) * 12.0
        if defl_in > 0.35 or sname in ("W01", "W02", "W03", "W08"):
            print(f"  {sname} {aname}: {defl_in:.4f} in (u_mean={u_mean*12:.4f} in)")

print("\n=== ZONE MAX UNIT SHEAR (plf) across all 12 scenarios ===")
zone_max_v = {z: 0.0 for z in z_all}
for i, j, xc, yc, zid, enodes in cells:
    Ghat = 12.0 * zone_Gp[zid]
    dN_dx = np.array([-1, 1, 1, -1]) / (2.0 * 5.0)
    dN_dy = np.array([-1, -1, 1, 1]) / (2.0 * 5.0)
    for s_idx in range(len(scenarios)):
        u = U_all[:, s_idx]
        gamma = sum(dN_dy[a]*u[2*enodes[a]] + dN_dx[a]*u[2*enodes[a]+1] for a in range(4))
        v = abs(Ghat * gamma) * 1000.0
        zone_max_v[zid] = max(zone_max_v[zid], v)
for z in z_all:
    print(f"  {z}: {zone_max_v[z]:.1f} plf")

print("\n=== CHORD MAX FORCES (kips, tension / compression / abs) ===")
for cid, _, _, _ in chord_lines:
    max_t, max_c, max_abs = 0.0, 0.0, 0.0
    for s_idx in range(len(scenarios)):
        u = U_all[:, s_idx]
        for n1, n2, ax, k_bar in bar_elems[cid]:
            f = k_bar * (u[2*n2+ax] - u[2*n1+ax])
            if f > max_t: max_t = f
            if -f > max_c: max_c = -f
            if abs(f) > max_abs: max_abs = abs(f)
    print(f"  {cid:5s}: max_abs={max_abs:6.2f} kips (T={max_t:6.2f}, C={max_c:6.2f})")
EOF

EOR-NDDC-A2-S01 — Structural Design Criteria: Roof Diaphragm and
Perimeter Shear Walls
Northern Divide Data Campus, Building A2 · Lewis and Clark County, Montana · Kestrel Ridge Structural Engineers, PLLC · Revision 2, 14
August 2026 · supersedes Revision 0 of 3 May 2024
1. Scope
This criteria governs the design of the Building A2 roof deck diaphragm, its chords and collectors, the precast perimeter
shear wall panels and their connections, for wind loading. It is issued to the delegated engineer with the boundary-layer
wind study WT-2026-07, the as-built federated model, the catalogues named in section 12, and the submittal
specification 01 33 00.
Seismic design of Building A2 is governed separately by EOR-NDDC-A2-S02 and is not part of this package. The site is
Seismic Design Category B and wind governs the lateral design of this building in both directions.
2. Governing code
2021 International Building Code as adopted by the State of Montana (ARM 24.301.131), with ASCE/SEI 7-16 as the
referenced load standard. Risk Category III per the Authority Having Jurisdiction's letter NDDC-AHJ-014. Deflection
criteria are taken as the more restrictive of the governing code and UFC 3-301-01 Table 2-1, which the Owner's Basis
of Design adopts for this campus.
3. Load basis and reporting
3.1 Wind loads are determined at strength level from the basic wind speed of section 4 and the pressure coefficients of
the wind study.
3.2 Wind is the only lateral load considered in this package. Gravity load effects on the diaphragm are not combined
with in-plane wind shear; dead load enters only the panel stability check of 5.8.
3.3 Every quantity reported in this submittal - diaphragm unit shears, wall line loads and reactions, chord and
collector forces, deflections - is an ALLOWABLE STRESS DESIGN quantity, obtained from the strength-level
wind effect by the load combination 0.6W. Member and connection capacities are compared against it on the
same basis. The drawings and the calculation package must state on their face that the loads shown are ASD.
4. Wind parameters
4.1 Exposure Category C, open terrain, in all directions. Enclosure classification: enclosed, GCpi = ±0.18. Internal
pressure acts on opposite internal faces simultaneously and therefore cancels in the net lateral force on the main wind
force resisting system; it is not to be included in the diaphragm and shear wall loads. It is included in the out-of-plane
panel design, which is a separate submittal.
4.2 The velocity pressure at elevation z is
    q(z) = 0.00256 * Kz(z) * Kzt * Kd * Ke * V^2      [psf, V in mph]
    Kz(z) = 2.01 * (z / 900)^(2/9.5),  z not taken less than 15 ft
with Kd = 0.85 and V from the AHJ letter. q_h is q(z) evaluated at the mean roof height; the velocity pressure for a
parapet is evaluated at the top of that parapet.
4.3 The topographic factor Kzt is taken from the site-specific study TS-2026-02 and applies over the whole footprint.
Revision 0 of this criteria carried Kzt = 1.00 and a basic wind speed of 105 mph; both were superseded when
the topographic study and the AHJ letter were issued.
4.4 The ground elevation factor is
    Ke = exp(-0.0000362 * zg)      zg = site ground elevation above sea level, ft
with zg taken from the ALTA survey benchmark. Ke is not to be taken as 1.0 at this site.

The wall lines are identified S (south, y = 0), E (east, x = 240), N1 (north, y = 180), W (west, x = 0), and, on the
generator yard, N2 (y = 140) and E2 (x = 180).
5. Precast wall panels
5.1 The perimeter walls are precast concrete panels spanning vertically between the foundation and the roof deck, with
a parapet cantilevering above the deck. Panel-to-panel joints transfer no in-plane shear: each panel resists in-plane
force independently.
5.2 Panel concrete f'c = 5000 psi, Ec = 4030 ksi, G = 0.40 Ec, unit weight 150 pcf.
5.3 Panel geometry - mark, length, thickness, top elevation and openings - is taken from the as-built federated model
and the roof line scan. Where the 2024 precast panel schedule and the as-built model disagree, the as-built model
governs and the difference is to be reported in the design basis.
5.4 Openings divide a panel into vertical legs. A leg is the full-height strip of panel between an opening edge and the
next opening edge or panel edge. A leg narrower than 2.0 ft is neglected: it is assigned no stiffness and carries no
in-plane shear.
5.5 Each leg is idealised as a cantilever pier fixed at the foundation and free at the roof deck, of height h equal to the
roof deck elevation, with
    k = 1 / ( h^3 / (3 Ec I) + 1.2 h / (G A) )        [kip/in]
    I = t L^3 / 12,   A = t L,   t = panel thickness, L = leg length
with h, t and L in inches. The parapet above the deck contributes no in-plane stiffness.
5.6 A panel's in-plane shear is the sum of the shears of its legs.
5.7 The panel base connection to the foundation has the ASD shear capacity per foot of panel length given in the
connection vendor data; the demand is the panel's in-plane shear.
5.8 Panel stability is checked with the ASD combination 0.6D + 0.6W: the overturning moment is the panel's ASD
in-plane shear times the roof deck elevation, and the resisting moment is 0.6 times the panel self weight times half the
panel length. Where the resisting moment is insufficient, a base tie-down assembly is provided; the assembly's ASD
capacity acts at a lever arm equal to the panel length. Panel self weight is computed on the GROSS panel area - full
panel length by top elevation by thickness - with no deduction for openings.
6. Wind pressures and the roof-level wall line load
6.1 The wind study reports a pressure coefficient for each facade patch and each azimuth, referenced to q_h. The
design pressure on a wall patch is p = q_h * Cp. The net pressure on a parapet patch is p = q_p * GCpn, with q_p the

--- Page 3 ---
EOR-NDDC-A2-S01 Structural Design Criteria Rev 2
page 3
velocity pressure at the top of that parapet and GCpn the study's net parapet coefficient; the parapet coefficient already
includes both faces.
6.2 Patch geometry is not tabulated in the wind study. A patch covers the full length of the panel it names and the
elevation band its identifier names; the bands are defined in the wind study. Panel lengths and top elevations come
from the as-built model.
6.3 Wall pressures act on the gross wall area, including door and louver openings; the door and louver framing delivers
its reaction to the surrounding panel.
6.4 Each panel spans vertically as a simple beam between the foundation and the roof deck. A patch pressure
p acting on an area A whose centroid is at elevation z therefore delivers
    R_roof = p * A * z / h        to the roof deck, and
    R_base = p * A * (1 - z/h)    to the foundation
with h the roof deck elevation. A patch above the deck - a parapet or a screen wall - has z > h, so it delivers
MORE than its own force to the diaphragm and an uplift-sense reaction at the base: this is the lever action of
the wall cantilevering above the diaphragm and it is not to be omitted. The roof-level line load on a wall line is the
sum of R_roof over the patches of that line, per foot of wall.
6.5 The line load acts along the wall's inward normal.
6.6 Torsional case. For wind on either principal axis the diaphragm is also checked with all line loads factored by 0.75
together with a torsional moment
    M_T = e * B * |F|        e = +/- 0.15
where |F| is the magnitude of the factored resultant in the direction of the wind and B the horizontal building dimension
perpendicular to the wind (240 ft for wind on the north or south face, 180 ft for wind on the east or west face). M_T is
applied to the diaphragm as a set of in-plane nodal forces proportional to the nodal tributary area and to the distance
from the diaphragm area centroid, directed perpendicular to that radius, scaled so that their moment about the centroid
equals M_T.
7. Roof deck
7.1 The roof is divided into the deck zones shown on S-201. Exactly one deck type from the deck manufacturer's
catalogue is used over the whole of each zone.
7.2 The diaphragm unit shear anywhere within a zone must not exceed the ASD shear capacity of that zone's deck
type. The catalogue tabulates NOMINAL strengths; the safety factor for the ASD capacity is given in the catalogue's
notes.
7.3 The catalogue's shear stiffness G' is tabulated for the deck span stated in its notes; where the framing gives a
different deck span, the note's adjustment applies. The adjustment applies to stiffness only, never to strength.
8. Acceptance limits
8.1 All checks are on the ASD basis of 3.3.
8.2 Diaphragm deflection. For each scenario and each global axis, the deflection of the diaphragm relative to its
supports is the largest nodal displacement in that axis measured from the stiffness-weighted mean displacement of the
piers that resist that axis. It must not exceed 0.55 in, the value the Owner's Basis of Design sets for the precast
connection detail.
8.3 Pier drift must not exceed h / 400.
9. DIAPH-MT 1.0 - the required diaphragm analysis
The roof deck diaphragm is neither rigid nor flexible relative to the precast walls: the walls are stiff, the wall lines are not
collinear, and the re-entrant corner at the generator yard has no wall on two of its sides. A tributary (flexible) or a rigid
distribution is not accepted for this building. The following semi-rigid model is required, and the submitted
quantities are checked against it.

--- Page 4 ---
EOR-NDDC-A2-S01 Structural Design Criteria Rev 2
page 4
9.1 Mesh. A structured square mesh of side H is laid over the bounding rectangle of the roof, with its origin at the
building grid origin. A cell belongs to the diaphragm when its centre lies inside the roof outline and outside a roof
opening. Nodes are the corners of the cells that belong. Refinement levels: L1 H = 10.0 ft, L2 H = 5.0 ft, L3 H = 2.50 ft.
9.2 Elements. Each cell is a four-node bilinear membrane integrated with 2 x 2 Gauss quadrature, carrying the stress
resultants
    Nx  = EAx * eps_x        Ny = EAy * eps_y        Nxy = Ghat * gamma
    Ghat = 12 * G'           [kip/ft, with G' in kip/in]
EAx and EAy are the smeared axial rigidity of the roof framing, in kips per foot of width, computed as the chord area of
the member divided by its spacing times Es = 29,000 ksi - the girders east-west and the joists north-south, both from
the framing plan and the joist schedule. The deck itself is not credited with axial rigidity.
9.3 Chords and collectors are two-node bar elements of area A and Es = 29,000 ksi on the lines of section 10, one
bar per mesh interval, acting in the direction of the line.
9.4 Supports. Each pier of 5.5 is a spring of stiffness k acting in the plane of its wall, attached at the mesh node
nearest the mid-point of the leg. Where two piers resolve to the same node their stiffnesses add.
9.5 Loads. The roof-level line load of 6.4 is applied to the perimeter nodes of its wall line as the consistent nodal loads
of the piecewise-linear hat functions between adjacent nodes on that line.
9.6 Recovery. The diaphragm unit shear of an element is Ghat times the engineering shear strain at the element
centre. The unit shear reported at a station on a wall line is that of the element which has an edge on that wall line and
whose centre is nearest the station. A wall line's reaction is the sum of its piers' spring forces. A chord or collector force
is the largest bar force on that line.
9.7 Mesh convergence. The model is run at all three levels. The convergence measure is the relative change between
L2 and L3 in the reaction of wall line W under scenario W01, which must not exceed 5 %. The largest unit shear in the
building is a corner quantity and does not converge at that rate; report it at each level, but do not use it as the
convergence measure. Level L2 is the level at which the submitted quantities are reported and checked.

1. Scope
A pressure-model study of Building A2 in its as-built massing, including the generator-yard re-entrant corner and the
mechanical screen wall, to provide main wind force resisting system pressure coefficients for the roof diaphragm and
shear wall design.
2. Model and instrumentation
Rigid pressure model at 1:200, 512 surface taps on the four elevations and the two notch elevations, sampled at 512 Hz
for 180 s at each azimuth, 36 azimuths at 10 degree increments. Results are reported at the eight cardinal and
intercardinal azimuths, which envelope the measured set for every wall line.
3. Reference pressure
Every coefficient in this report and in the accompanying data file is referenced to the velocity pressure at mean
roof height, q_h. The height variation of the windward pressure is contained in the reported coefficients; the design
pressure on a wall patch is p = q_h * Cp and no further height adjustment is to be applied.
4. Azimuth convention
An azimuth is the direction the wind comes FROM, measured clockwise from north: 0 degrees is a wind from the north
blowing toward the south, 90 degrees is a wind from the east.
5. Patch convention
The facade is divided into patches. A patch covers the full length of one precast panel and one elevation band. The
bands are B1 = 0 to 7 ft, B2 = 7 to 14 ft, B3 = 14 to 21 ft, B4 = 21 to 28 ft, and the band identified P is the parapet - the
strip from the roof deck to the top of that panel, whatever its height. A patch identifier is the panel mark followed by
the band: S06-B3 is panel S06 between 14 and 21 ft, N108-P is the parapet strip of panel N108. Panel lengths and
top elevations are not reproduced here; they are properties of the as-built model.
6. Coefficients
6.1 Wall patches. The data file gives the mean pressure coefficient Cp for each wall patch and azimuth. Positive is
toward the surface.
6.2 The re-entrant corner of the generator yard produces a locally amplified suction on the two notch elevations at every
azimuth; that amplification is in the reported coefficients.
6.3 Parapet patches. For a parapet the data file gives the NET coefficient GCpn, which acts on the parapet's projected
area and already accounts for both faces: +1.5 on a windward parapet and -1.0 on a leeward parapet, interpolated on
the cosine of the incidence for an oblique wind. The net parapet pressure is p = q_p * GCpn with q_p the velocity
pressure at the top of that parapet, not at mean roof height - the screen wall on the north elevation reaches well
above the deck and its velocity pressure is correspondingly higher.
6.4 Internal pressure is not part of this study.
7. Data file
WT-2026-07_Cp_by_azimuth.csv, columns patch_id, azimuth_deg, cp. One row per patch per azimuth.
8. Uncertainty

page 2
The tap-to-tap repeatability of the reported means is +/- 0.03 in Cp. The coefficients are reported to four decimal places
for traceability, not because they are known to that precision.

--- Page 1 ---
WT-2026-07 Boundary Layer Wind Study
page 1
WT-2026-07 — Boundary Layer Wind Study, Building A2
Sawtooth Wind Engineering · final report · 22 July 2026 · 1:200 scale rigid model, suburban-to-open rural approach, Exposure C target profile
1. Scope
A pressure-model study of Building A2 in its as-built massing, including the generator-yard re-entrant corner and the
mechanical screen wall, to provide main wind force resisting system pressure coefficients for the roof diaphragm and
shear wall design.
2. Model and instrumentation
Rigid pressure model at 1:200, 512 surface taps on the four elevations and the two notch elevations, sampled at 512 Hz
for 180 s at each azimuth, 36 azimuths at 10 degree increments. Results are reported at the eight cardinal and
intercardinal azimuths, which envelope the measured set for every wall line.
3. Reference pressure
Every coefficient in this report and in the accompanying data file is referenced to the velocity pressure at mean
roof height, q_h. The height variation of the windward pressure is contained in the reported coefficients; the design
pressure on a wall patch is p = q_h * Cp and no further height adjustment is to be applied.
4. Azimuth convention
An azimuth is the direction the wind comes FROM, measured clockwise from north: 0 degrees is a wind from the north
blowing toward the south, 90 degrees is a wind from the east.
5. Patch convention
The facade is divided into patches. A patch covers the full length of one precast panel and one elevation band. The
bands are B1 = 0 to 7 ft, B2 = 7 to 14 ft, B3 = 14 to 21 ft, B4 = 21 to 28 ft, and the band identified P is the parapet - the
strip from the roof deck to the top of that panel, whatever its height. A patch identifier is the panel mark followed by
the band: S06-B3 is panel S06 between 14 and 21 ft, N108-P is the parapet strip of panel N108. Panel lengths and
top elevations are not reproduced here; they are properties of the as-built model.
6. Coefficients
6.1 Wall patches. The data file gives the mean pressure coefficient Cp for each wall patch and azimuth. Positive is
toward the surface.
6.2 The re-entrant corner of the generator yard produces a locally amplified suction on the two notch elevations at every
azimuth; that amplification is in the reported coefficients.
6.3 Parapet patches. For a parapet the data file gives the NET coefficient GCpn, which acts on the parapet's projected
area and already accounts for both faces: +1.5 on a windward parapet and -1.0 on a leeward parapet, interpolated on
the cosine of the incidence for an oblique wind. The net parapet pressure is p = q_p * GCpn with q_p the velocity
pressure at the top of that parapet, not at mean roof height - the screen wall on the north elevation reaches well
above the deck and its velocity pressure is correspondingly higher.
6.4 Internal pressure is not part of this study.
7. Data file
WT-2026-07_Cp_by_azimuth.csv, columns patch_id, azimuth_deg, cp. One row per patch per azimuth.
8. Uncertainty

--- Page 2 ---
WT-2026-07 Boundary Layer Wind Study
page 2
The tap-to-tap repeatability of the reported means is +/- 0.03 in Cp. The coefficients are reported to four decimal places
for traceability, not because they are known to that precision.
9. Limitations
The study covers the as-built massing of 2026. It does not cover the roof-mounted equipment, the screen wall's own
component-and-cladding pressures, or any future Building A3 to the east.

EOR-NDDC-A2-S01 Structural Design Criteria Rev 2
page 1
EOR-NDDC-A2-S01 — Structural Design Criteria: Roof Diaphragm and
Perimeter Shear Walls
Northern Divide Data Campus, Building A2 · Lewis and Clark County, Montana · Kestrel Ridge Structural Engineers, PLLC · Revision 2, 14
August 2026 · supersedes Revision 0 of 3 May 2024
1. Scope
This criteria governs the design of the Building A2 roof deck diaphragm, its chords and collectors, the precast perimeter
shear wall panels and their connections, for wind loading. It is issued to the delegated engineer with the boundary-layer
wind study WT-2026-07, the as-built federated model, the catalogues named in section 12, and the submittal
specification 01 33 00.
Seismic design of Building A2 is governed separately by EOR-NDDC-A2-S02 and is not part of this package. The site is
Seismic Design Category B and wind governs the lateral design of this building in both directions.
2. Governing code
2021 International Building Code as adopted by the State of Montana (ARM 24.301.131), with ASCE/SEI 7-16 as the
referenced load standard. Risk Category III per the Authority Having Jurisdiction's letter NDDC-AHJ-014. Deflection
criteria are taken as the more restrictive of the governing code and UFC 3-301-01 Table 2-1, which the Owner's Basis
of Design adopts for this campus.
3. Load basis and reporting
3.1 Wind loads are determined at strength level from the basic wind speed of section 4 and the pressure coefficients of
the wind study.
3.2 Wind is the only lateral load considered in this package. Gravity load effects on the diaphragm are not combined
with in-plane wind shear; dead load enters only the panel stability check of 5.8.
3.3 Every quantity reported in this submittal - diaphragm unit shears, wall line loads and reactions, chord and
collector forces, deflections - is an ALLOWABLE STRESS DESIGN quantity, obtained from the strength-level
wind effect by the load combination 0.6W. Member and connection capacities are compared against it on the
same basis. The drawings and the calculation package must state on their face that the loads shown are ASD.
4. Wind parameters
4.1 Exposure Category C, open terrain, in all directions. Enclosure classification: enclosed, GCpi = ±0.18. Internal
pressure acts on opposite internal faces simultaneously and therefore cancels in the net lateral force on the main wind
force resisting system; it is not to be included in the diaphragm and shear wall loads. It is included in the out-of-plane
panel design, which is a separate submittal.
4.2 The velocity pressure at elevation z is
    q(z) = 0.00256 * Kz(z) * Kzt * Kd * Ke * V^2      [psf, V in mph]
    Kz(z) = 2.01 * (z / 900)^(2/9.5),  z not taken less than 15 ft
with Kd = 0.85 and V from the AHJ letter. q_h is q(z) evaluated at the mean roof height; the velocity pressure for a
parapet is evaluated at the top of that parapet.
4.3 The topographic factor Kzt is taken from the site-specific study TS-2026-02 and applies over the whole footprint.
Revision 0 of this criteria carried Kzt = 1.00 and a basic wind speed of 105 mph; both were superseded when
the topographic study and the AHJ letter were issued.
4.4 The ground elevation factor is
    Ke = exp(-0.0000362 * zg)      zg = site ground elevation above sea level, ft
with zg taken from the ALTA survey benchmark. Ke is not to be taken as 1.0 at this site.

=== EOR Page 2 ===
EOR-NDDC-A2-S01 Structural Design Criteria Rev 2

building axes, with the torsional case of 6.6. The twelve scenarios are identified as follows, and every schedule and
drawing in the submittal refers to them by these identifiers.

The wall lines are identified S (south, y = 0), E (east, x = 240), N1 (north, y = 180), W (west, x = 0), and, on the
generator yard, N2 (y = 140) and E2 (x = 180).
5. Precast wall panels
5.1 The perimeter walls are precast concrete panels spanning vertically between the foundation and the roof deck, with
a parapet cantilevering above the deck. Panel-to-panel joints transfer no in-plane shear: each panel resists in-plane
force independently.
5.2 Panel concrete f'c = 5000 psi, Ec = 4030 ksi, G = 0.40 Ec, unit weight 150 pcf.
5.3 Panel geometry - mark, length, thickness, top elevation and openings - is taken from the as-built federated model
and the roof line scan. Where the 2024 precast panel schedule and the as-built model disagree, the as-built model
governs and the difference is to be reported in the design basis.
5.4 Openings divide a panel into vertical legs. A leg is the full-height strip of panel between an opening edge and the
next opening edge or panel edge. A leg narrower than 2.0 ft is neglected: it is assigned no stiffness and carries no
in-plane shear.
5.5 Each leg is idealised as a cantilever pier fixed at the foundation and free at the roof deck, of height h equal to the
roof deck elevation, with
    k = 1 / ( h^3 / (3 Ec I) + 1.2 h / (G A) )        [kip/in]
    I = t L^3 / 12,   A = t L,   t = panel thickness, L = leg length
with h, t and L in inches. The parapet above the deck contributes no in-plane stiffness.
5.6 A panel's in-plane shear is the sum of the shears of its legs.
5.7 The panel base connection to the foundation has the ASD shear capacity per foot of panel length given in the
connection vendor data; the demand is the panel's in-plane shear.
5.8 Panel stability is checked with the ASD combination 0.6D + 0.6W: the overturning moment is the panel's ASD
in-plane shear times the roof deck elevation, and the resisting moment is 0.6 times the panel self weight times half the
panel length. Where the resisting moment is insufficient, a base tie-down assembly is provided; the assembly's ASD
capacity acts at a lever arm equal to the panel length. Panel self weight is computed on the GROSS panel area - full
panel length by top elevation by thickness - with no deduction for openings.
6. Wind pressures and the roof-level wall line load
6.1 The wind study reports a pressure coefficient for each facade patch and each azimuth, referenced to q_h. The
design pressure on a wall patch is p = q_h * Cp. The net pressure on a parapet patch is p = q_p * GCpn, with q_p the

=== EOR Page 3 ===
EOR-NDDC-A2-S01 Structural Design Criteria Rev 2
page 3
velocity pressure at the top of that parapet and GCpn the study's net parapet coefficient; the parapet coefficient already
includes both faces.
6.2 Patch geometry is not tabulated in the wind study. A patch covers the full length of the panel it names and the
elevation band its identifier names; the bands are defined in the wind study. Panel lengths and top elevations come
from the as-built model.
6.3 Wall pressures act on the gross wall area, including door and louver openings; the door and louver framing delivers
its reaction to the surrounding panel.
6.4 Each panel spans vertically as a simple beam between the foundation and the roof deck. A patch pressure
p acting on an area A whose centroid is at elevation z therefore delivers
    R_roof = p * A * z / h        to the roof deck, and
    R_base = p * A * (1 - z/h)    to the foundation
with h the roof deck elevation. A patch above the deck - a parapet or a screen wall - has z > h, so it delivers
MORE than its own force to the diaphragm and an uplift-sense reaction at the base: this is the lever action of
the wall cantilevering above the diaphragm and it is not to be omitted. The roof-level line load on a wall line is the
sum of R_roof over the patches of that line, per foot of wall.
6.5 The line load acts along the wall's inward normal.
6.6 Torsional case. For wind on either principal axis the diaphragm is also checked with all line loads factored by 0.75
together with a torsional moment
    M_T = e * B * |F|        e = +/- 0.15
where |F| is the magnitude of the factored resultant in the direction of the wind and B the horizontal building dimension
perpendicular to the wind (240 ft for wind on the north or south face, 180 ft for wind on the east or west face). M_T is
applied to the diaphragm as a set of in-plane nodal forces proportional to the nodal tributary area and to the distance
from the diaphragm area centroid, directed perpendicular to that radius, scaled so that their moment about the centroid
equals M_T.
7. Roof deck
7.1 The roof is divided into the deck zones shown on S-201. Exactly one deck type from the deck manufacturer's
catalogue is used over the whole of each zone.
7.2 The diaphragm unit shear anywhere within a zone must not exceed the ASD shear capacity of that zone's deck
type. The catalogue tabulates NOMINAL strengths; the safety factor for the ASD capacity is given in the catalogue's
notes.
7.3 The catalogue's shear stiffness G' is tabulated for the deck span stated in its notes; where the framing gives a
different deck span, the note's adjustment applies. The adjustment applies to stiffness only, never to strength.
8. Acceptance limits
8.1 All checks are on the ASD basis of 3.3.
8.2 Diaphragm deflection. For each scenario and each global axis, the deflection of the diaphragm relative to its
supports is the largest nodal displacement in that axis measured from the stiffness-weighted mean displacement of the
piers that resist that axis. It must not exceed 0.55 in, the value the Owner's Basis of Design sets for the precast
connection detail.
8.3 Pier drift must not exceed h / 400.
9. DIAPH-MT 1.0 - the required diaphragm analysis
The roof deck diaphragm is neither rigid nor flexible relative to the precast walls: the walls are stiff, the wall lines are not
collinear, and the re-entrant corner at the generator yard has no wall on two of its sides. A tributary (flexible) or a rigid
distribution is not accepted for this building. The following semi-rigid model is required, and the submitted
quantities are checked against it.

=== EOR Page 4 ===
EOR-NDDC-A2-S01 Structural Design Criteria Rev 2
page 4
9.1 Mesh. A structured square mesh of side H is laid over the bounding rectangle of the roof, with its origin at the
building grid origin. A cell belongs to the diaphragm when its centre lies inside the roof outline and outside a roof
opening. Nodes are the corners of the cells that belong. Refinement levels: L1 H = 10.0 ft, L2 H = 5.0 ft, L3 H = 2.50 ft.
9.2 Elements. Each cell is a four-node bilinear membrane integrated with 2 x 2 Gauss quadrature, carrying the stress
resultants
    Nx  = EAx * eps_x        Ny = EAy * eps_y        Nxy = Ghat * gamma
    Ghat = 12 * G'           [kip/ft, with G' in kip/in]
EAx and EAy are the smeared axial rigidity of the roof framing, in kips per foot of width, computed as the chord area of
the member divided by its spacing times Es = 29,000 ksi - the girders east-west and the joists north-south, both from
the framing plan and the joist schedule. The deck itself is not credited with axial rigidity.
9.3 Chords and collectors are two-node bar elements of area A and Es = 29,000 ksi on the lines of section 10, one
bar per mesh interval, acting in the direction of the line.
9.4 Supports. Each pier of 5.5 is a spring of stiffness k acting in the plane of its wall, attached at the mesh node
nearest the mid-point of the leg. Where two piers resolve to the same node their stiffnesses add.
9.5 Loads. The roof-level line load of 6.4 is applied to the perimeter nodes of its wall line as the consistent nodal loads
of the piecewise-linear hat functions between adjacent nodes on that line.
9.6 Recovery. The diaphragm unit shear of an element is Ghat times the engineering shear strain at the element
centre. The unit shear reported at a station on a wall line is that of the element which has an edge on that wall line and
whose centre is nearest the station. A wall line's reaction is the sum of its piers' spring forces. A chord or collector force
is the largest bar force on that line.
9.7 Mesh convergence. The model is run at all three levels. The convergence measure is the relative change between
L2 and L3 in the reaction of wall line W under scenario W01, which must not exceed 5 %. The largest unit shear in the
building is a corner quantity and does not converge at that rate; report it at each level, but do not use it as the
convergence measure. Level L2 is the level at which the submitted quantities are reported and checked.
9.8 Verification example VE-1
An implementation of DIAPH-MT must reproduce the following before it is applied to Building A2. A rectangular
diaphragm 100 ft (east-west) by 60 ft (north-south), mesh H = 5.0 ft, one deck type with G' = 30.0 kip/in everywhere (no
span adjustment), EAx = 2,900 and EAy = 13,920 kip/ft, chord bars of A = 3.00 in² on all four edges, and twelve piers
each of k = 500 kip/in: four on the y = 0 line and four on the y = 60 line at x = 12.5, 37.5, 62.5 and 87.5 ft resisting X,
and two on the x = 0 line and two on the x = 100 line at y = 15 and 45 ft resisting Y. Loads: a uniform inward line load of
0.50 kip/ft on the y = 0 line and 0.30 kip/ft on the y = 60 line, both at strength level, no torsional case.

10. Chords and collectors
10.1 Chord and collector lines are shown on S-201 and are listed there with their identifiers. Every line carries a section
from the chord and collector schedule over its full length.
10.2 Chord force is the axial force in the chord bar; tension and compression are checked against the schedule's
allowable values.

EOR-NDDC-A2-S01 Structural Design Criteria Rev 2
page 5
10.3 The collector lines at the re-entrant corner drag diaphragm shear into the walls of the generator yard; the lines
around the mechanical well transfer shear around the opening. Both are checked as 10.2.
11. Submittal
11.1 A calculation package on 8-1/2 x 11 sheets, portrait, covering: the wind pressures; the parapet cantilever transfer
to the roof deck; the diaphragm reactions; the diaphragm shears; the chord forces; the shear wall loads; and the design
basis.
11.2 Plan view drawings of the roof showing the diaphragm unit shear distribution and the shear wall reactions for both
the transverse and the longitudinal direction, with the deck zones, the chord and collector lines, the building grid and the
annotation required by specification 01 33 00.
11.2.1 Report stations. The diaphragm unit shear is reported at the quarter points of every wall line - the station
fractions 0.25, 0.50, 0.75 of the line's length, measured from the start of the line as section 4.5 sets it out - for every
wind scenario. The unit shear at a station is recovered as 9.6 defines it.
11.3 Schedules of the reported quantities. The Engineer of Record re-runs DIAPH-MT on the submitted design;
reported quantities are accepted when they agree within 7.5 % or 25 plf / 2 kips / 0.05 in, whichever is larger.

WT-2026-07 — Boundary Layer Wind Study, Building A2
Sawtooth Wind Engineering · final report · 22 July 2026 · 1:200 scale rigid model, suburban-to-open rural approach, Exposure C target profile
1. Scope
A pressure-model study of Building A2 in its as-built massing, including the generator-yard re-entrant corner and the
mechanical screen wall, to provide main wind force resisting system pressure coefficients for the roof diaphragm and
shear wall design.
2. Model and instrumentation
Rigid pressure model at 1:200, 512 surface taps on the four elevations and the two notch elevations, sampled at 512 Hz
for 180 s at each azimuth, 36 azimuths at 10 degree increments. Results are reported at the eight cardinal and
intercardinal azimuths, which envelope the measured set for every wall line.
3. Reference pressure
Every coefficient in this report and in the accompanying data file is referenced to the velocity pressure at mean
roof height, q_h. The height variation of the windward pressure is contained in the reported coefficients; the design
pressure on a wall patch is p = q_h * Cp and no further height adjustment is to be applied.
4. Azimuth convention
An azimuth is the direction the wind comes FROM, measured clockwise from north: 0 degrees is a wind from the north
blowing toward the south, 90 degrees is a wind from the east.
5. Patch convention
The facade is divided into patches. A patch covers the full length of one precast panel and one elevation band. The
bands are B1 = 0 to 7 ft, B2 = 7 to 14 ft, B3 = 14 to 21 ft, B4 = 21 to 28 ft, and the band identified P is the parapet - the
strip from the roof deck to the top of that panel, whatever its height. A patch identifier is the panel mark followed by
the band: S06-B3 is panel S06 between 14 and 21 ft, N108-P is the parapet strip of panel N108. Panel lengths and
top elevations are not reproduced here; they are properties of the as-built model.
6. Coefficients
6.1 Wall patches. The data file gives the mean pressure coefficient Cp for each wall patch and azimuth. Positive is
toward the surface.
6.2 The re-entrant corner of the generator yard produces a locally amplified suction on the two notch elevations at every
azimuth; that amplification is in the reported coefficients.
6.3 Parapet patches. For a parapet the data file gives the NET coefficient GCpn, which acts on the parapet's projected
area and already accounts for both faces: +1.5 on a windward parapet and -1.0 on a leeward parapet, interpolated on
the cosine of the incidence for an oblique wind. The net parapet pressure is p = q_p * GCpn with q_p the velocity
pressure at the top of that parapet, not at mean roof height - the screen wall on the north elevation reaches well
above the deck and its velocity pressure is correspondingly higher.
6.4 Internal pressure is not part of this study.
7. Data file
WT-2026-07_Cp_by_azimuth.csv, columns patch_id, azimuth_deg, cp. One row per patch per azimuth.
8. Uncertainty

WT-2026-07 Boundary Layer Wind Study
page 2
The tap-to-tap repeatability of the reported means is +/- 0.03 in Cp. The coefficients are reported to four decimal places
for traceability, not because they are known to that precision.
9. Limitations
The study covers the as-built massing of 2026. It does not cover the roof-mounted equipment, the screen wall's own
component-and-cladding pressures, or any future Building A3 to the east.

# Building A2 — Lateral Package Design Basis Narrative

**Project:** Northern Divide Data Campus — Building A2 (Lewis and Clark County, Montana)  
**Permit Application:** 2026-0418  
**Engineer of Record:** Kestrel Ridge Structural Engineers, PLLC  
**Governing Structural Criteria:** `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Revision 2 (12 May 2026)  

---

## 1. Summary of Wind Load and Geometric Design Basis Parameters

In accordance with Specification `01 33 00` Section 1.5, Table 1 below records the governing design basis parameters, their adopted values, and the authoritative source documents from which they are derived.

## 2. Governing Wind Scenario by Shear Wall Line

In accordance with Specification `01 33 00` Section 1.5, Table 2 below identifies the governing wind scenario (out of `W01` through `W12`) that produces the maximum in-plane diaphragm reaction on each exterior shear wall line.

| line | governing scenario |
| --- | --- |
| S | W07 |
| E | W10 |
| N1 | W07 |
| W | W01 |
| N2 | W03 |
| E2 | W01 |

---

## 3. Resolution of Document Conflicts and Superseded Revisions

In accordance with Specification `01 33 00` Sections 1.5 and 1.7 and Document Transmittal `T-204`, the following conflicts between issued documents, field surveys, and archived/superseded files were identified and resolved:

1. **Risk Category and Basic Wind Speed (`NDDC-AHJ-014` & `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Rev 2 vs. Superseded 2024 Pre-Application Memo & `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Rev 0):**  
   The superseded 2024 pre-application wind note and archived criteria `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Rev 0 (EOR-NDDC-A2-S01 Rev0) specified Risk Category II with an ultimate basic wind speed of `V = 105 mph`. In letter `NDDC-AHJ-014` (11 June 2026), the Lewis and Clark County Building Division classified Building A2 in **Risk Category III** (consistent with `UFC 3-301-01` Table 2-2 for mission-essential data handling facilities) with an ultimate basic wind speed of **`V = 115 mph`**, Exposure Category C, and `Kd = 0.85`. `NDDC-AHJ-014` and `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Rev 2 govern.

2. **Topographic Wind Speedup Factor (`TS-2026-02` & `NDDC-AHJ-014` vs. Superseded `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Rev 0):**  
   Superseded criteria `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Rev 0 assumed a flat site with `Kzt = 1.00`. The site-specific topographic study `TS-2026-02` established that Building A2 sits 220 ft downwind of a 110 ft escarpment (`H/Lh = 0.20`), yielding **`Kzt = 1.19`** at `z = 28 ft` across all wind azimuths, which the AHJ mandated in `NDDC-AHJ-014` Clause 4 and `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Rev 2 Clause 4.3.

3. **As-Built Roof Footprint, Generator Yard Notch, and Mechanical Well Opening (`NDDC-A2_Federated_Model_2026.ifc`, `ALTA-2025-77`, `A-101` Rev C, & `S-201` Rev C vs. Superseded `A-101` Rev A & `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Rev 0):**  
   Superseded architectural plan `A-101` Rev A (A-101 RevA) and `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Rev 0 depicted Building A2 as a clean 240 ft by 180 ft rectangle (`43,200 sf`) with no roof openings and only four exterior wall lines (`S, E, N, W`). The 2026 as-built survey (`ALTA-2025-77`), federated BIM model (`NDDC-A2_Federated_Model_2026.ifc`), `A-101` Rev C, and `S-201` Rev C establish that the building has a **60 ft by 40 ft re-entrant generator yard notch** at the north-east corner (`x = 180..240 ft, y = 140..180 ft`, bounded by shear wall lines `N2` at `y = 140 ft` and `E2` at `x = 180 ft`) and a **40 ft by 30 ft mechanical well roof opening** (`x = 100..140 ft, y = 100..130 ft`, `1,200 sf`), resulting in a net roof deck diaphragm area of **`39,600 sf`**. The 2026 as-built geometry governs.

4. **North Mechanical Screen Wall Elevation (`NDDC-A2_Federated_Model_2026.ifc`, `SR-2026-118`, `Roof_Line_Scan_2026-08-14.ply`, `A-301` Rev C, & `PC-S02` Rev 2 vs. `PC-S01` 2024 Schedule & Superseded `PC-S02` Rev 1):**  
   The 2024 precast fabrication schedule `PC-S01_Precast_Panel_Schedule_2024.xlsx` and superseded elevation drawing `PC-S02` Rev 1 listed a uniform panel top elevation of `31.0 ft` (`3.0 ft` parapet above the `28.0 ft` roof deck) for all 63 panels, including north wall panels `N108, N109, N110, N111`. However, the 2026 LiDAR roof line scan (`SR-2026-118` and `Roof_Line_Scan_2026-08-14.ply`), the 2026 federated model (`NDDC-A2_Federated_Model_2026.ifc`), `OBD-NDDC-A2` Clause 4.3, `A-301` Rev C, and `PC-S02` Rev 2 confirm that panels **`N108, N109, N110, N111`** (`x = 96.0 ft` to `168.0 ft` on line `N1`) extend to **`top_z = 36.0 ft` AFF** (`8.0 ft` integral screen wall cantilevering above the `28.0 ft` roof deck). Per `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Clause 5.3 and `Spec 01 33 00` Clause 1.7, `top_z = 36.0 ft` governs for `N108–N111`, increasing both the wind cantilever reaction delivered to the roof diaphragm (`q_p(36) = 30.31 psf` over an `8.0 ft` height with centroid at `z = 32.0 ft`, lever ratio `32.0 / 28.0 = 1.1429`) and the gross panel self-weight resisting overturning.

5. **Field-Cut Doorway Opening `S14-O1` in Panel `S14` and Neglect of Narrow Pier Leg (`NDDC-A2_Federated_Model_2026.ifc` & `PC-S02` Rev 2 vs. `PC-S01` 2024 Schedule & Superseded `PC-S02` Rev 1):**  
   The 2024 schedule `PC-S01` and superseded `PC-S02` Rev 1 listed panel `S14` (`x = 192.0..204.0 ft` on wall line `S`) as a solid panel (`openings = none`). The 2026 federated model (`NDDC-A2_Federated_Model_2026.ifc`, element `S14-O1`) and `PC-S02` Rev 2 document an **8.0 ft wide by 12.0 ft high doorway field-cut after erection** from `x = 194.5 ft` to `202.5 ft`. This opening divides panel `S14` into a west leg of width `194.5 - 192.0 = 2.5 ft` (`>= 2.0 ft`, valid pier with `k = 30.89 kip/in`) and an east leg of width `204.0 - 202.5 = 1.5 ft`. Per `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Clause 5.4, any leg narrower than `2.0 ft` is neglected and assigned zero stiffness (`k = 0`). The gross panel self-weight of `S14` is retained without deduction for openings per Clause 5.8.

6. **Diaphragm Analysis Methodology and Exclusion of Hall B Study (`NDDC-AHJ-014` Clause 3 & `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Rev 2 Section 9 vs. `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Rev 0 & `HallB_Lateral_Study_2023`):**  
   Superseded criteria `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Rev 0 and the archived study `HallB_Lateral_Study_2023` (which pertains to a different building, Hall B, on the campus) used a flexible-diaphragm tributary area method and omitted parapet cantilever amplification. Both `NDDC-AHJ-014` Clause 3 and `EOR-NDDC-A2-S01` Rev 2 Section 9 explicitly reject flexible or rigid distributions and mandate the **semi-rigid finite element procedure `DIAPH-MT 1.0`** together with full simple-beam parapet cantilever transfer (`R_roof = p * A * z / h`). `HallB_Lateral_Study_2023` is excluded in its entirety.

7. **Owner's Basis of Design Constraints (`OBD-NDDC-A2` Clauses 4.4–4.8):**  
   Per `OBD-NDDC-A2`, the roof deck is specified as primed steel deck only (acoustic deck is not required in data halls, Clause 4.5), limited to at most 4 distinct deck types across the roof (3 types used: `D22-36/4-4`, `D22-36/7-2`, `D22-36/7-4`, Clause 4.6), designed to hold diaphragm relative deflection within `0.55 in` (`0.5342 in` maximum achieved, Clause 4.4), and kept below the `$310,000` installed cost cap (`$215,683.74` total installed cost achieved, Clause 4.7). Commissioning (`OBD-NDDC-A2` Clause 4.8) is excluded from the structural package.

---

## 4. Explicit Scope Exclusions

- Flexible-diaphragm tributary distribution analysis is explicitly rejected by AHJ (NDDC-AHJ-014 Clause 3); semi-rigid diaphragm analysis per structural design criteria is required.
- Acoustic roof deck is not required in the data halls (OBD-NDDC-A2 Clause 4.5; primed deck only).
- Commissioning (OBD-NDDC-A2 Clause 4.8) is excluded from the structural package.
- 2024 clean-rectangle geometry and superseded archive files (A-101 RevA, EOR-NDDC-A2-S01 Rev0, PC-S02 Rev1, HallB_Lateral_Study_2023) are excluded in favor of 2026 federated model, roof line scan, and RevC/Rev2 documents.

page 1
EOR-NDDC-A2-S01 — Structural Design Criteria: Roof Diaphragm and
Perimeter Shear Walls
Northern Divide Data Campus, Building A2 · Lewis and Clark County, Montana · Kestrel Ridge Structural Engineers, PLLC · Revision 2, 14
August 2026 · supersedes Revision 0 of 3 May 2024
1. Scope
This criteria governs the design of the Building A2 roof deck diaphragm, its chords and collectors, the precast perimeter
shear wall panels and their connections, for wind loading. It is issued to the delegated engineer with the boundary-layer
wind study WT-2026-07, the as-built federated model, the catalogues named in section 12, and the submittal
specification 01 33 00.
Seismic design of Building A2 is governed separately by EOR-NDDC-A2-S02 and is not part of this package. The site is
Seismic Design Category B and wind governs the lateral design of this building in both directions.
2. Governing code
2021 International Building Code as adopted by the State of Montana (ARM 24.301.131), with ASCE/SEI 7-16 as the
referenced load standard. Risk Category III per the Authority Having Jurisdiction's letter NDDC-AHJ-014. Deflection
criteria are taken as the more restrictive of the governing code and UFC 3-301-01 Table 2-1, which the Owner's Basis
of Design adopts for this campus.
3. Load basis and reporting
3.1 Wind loads are determined at strength level from the basic wind speed of section 4 and the pressure coefficients of
the wind study.
3.2 Wind is the only lateral load considered in this package. Gravity load effects on the diaphragm are not combined
with in-plane wind shear; dead load enters only the panel stability check of 5.8.
3.3 Every quantity reported in this submittal - diaphragm unit shears, wall line loads and reactions, chord and
collector forces, deflections - is an ALLOWABLE STRESS DESIGN quantity, obtained from the strength-level
wind effect by the load combination 0.6W. Member and connection capacities are compared against it on the
same basis. The drawings and the calculation package must state on their face that the loads shown are ASD.
4. Wind parameters
4.1 Exposure Category C, open terrain, in all directions. Enclosure classification: enclosed, GCpi = ±0.18. Internal
pressure acts on opposite internal faces simultaneously and therefore cancels in the net lateral force on the main wind
force resisting system; it is not to be included in the diaphragm and shear wall loads. It is included in the out-of-plane
panel design, which is a separate submittal.

1. Scope
This criteria governs the design of the Building A2 roof deck diaphragm, its chords and collectors, the precast perimeter
shear wall panels and their connections, for wind loading. It is issued to the delegated engineer with the boundary-layer
wind study WT-2026-07, the as-built federated model, the catalogues named in section 12, and the submittal
specification 01 33 00.
Seismic design of Building A2 is governed separately by EOR-NDDC-A2-S02 and is not part of this package. The site is
Seismic Design Category B and wind governs the lateral design of this building in both directions.
2. Governing code
2021 International Building Code as adopted by the State of Montana (ARM 24.301.131), with ASCE/SEI 7-16 as the
referenced load standard. Risk Category III per the Authority Having Jurisdiction's letter NDDC-AHJ-014. Deflection
criteria are taken as the more restrictive of the governing code and UFC 3-301-01 Table 2-1, which the Owner's Basis
of Design adopts for this campus.
3. Load basis and reporting
3.1 Wind loads are determined at strength level from the basic wind speed of section 4 and the pressure coefficients of
the wind study.
3.2 Wind is the only lateral load considered in this package. Gravity load effects on the diaphragm are not combined
with in-plane wind shear; dead load enters only the panel stability check of 5.8.
3.3 Every quantity reported in this submittal - diaphragm unit shears, wall line loads and reactions, chord and
--- Page 1 ---
WT-2026-07 Boundary Layer Wind Study
page 1
WT-2026-07 — Boundary Layer Wind Study, Building A2
Sawtooth Wind Engineering · final report · 22 July 2026 · 1:200 scale rigid model, suburban-to-open rural approach, Exposure C target profile
1. Scope
A pressure-model study of Building A2 in its as-built massing, including the generator-yard re-entrant corner and the
mechanical screen wall, to provide main wind force resisting system pressure coefficients for the roof diaphragm and
shear wall design.
2. Model and instrumentation
Rigid pressure model at 1:200, 512 surface taps on the four elevations and the two notch elevations, sampled at 512 Hz
for 180 s at each azimuth, 36 azimuths at 10 degree increments. Results are reported at the eight cardinal and
intercardinal azimuths, which envelope the measured set for every wall line.
3. Reference pressure
Every coefficient in this report and in the accompanying data file is referenced to the velocity pressure at mean
roof height, q_h. The height variation of the windward pressure is contained in the reported coefficients; the design
pressure on a wall patch is p = q_h * Cp and no further height adjustment is to be applied.
4. Azimuth convention
An azimuth is the direction the wind comes FROM, measured clockwise from north: 0 degrees is a wind from the north
blowing toward the south, 90 degrees is a wind from the east.
5. Patch convention
The facade is divided into patches. A patch covers the full length of one precast panel and one elevation band. The
bands are B1 = 0 to 7 ft, B2 = 7 to 14 ft, B3 = 14 to 21 ft, B4 = 21 to 28 ft, and the band identified P is the parapet - the
strip from the roof deck to the top of that panel, whatever its height. A patch identifier is the panel mark followed by
the band: S06-B3 is panel S06 between 14 and 21 ft, N108-P is the parapet strip of panel N108. Panel lengths and
top elevations are not reproduced here; they are properties of the as-built model.
6. Coefficients
6.1 Wall patches. The data file gives the mean pressure coefficient Cp for each wall patch and azimuth. Positive is
toward the surface.
6.2 The re-entrant corner of the generator yard produces a locally amplified suction on the two notch elevations at every
azimuth; that amplification is in the reported coefficients.
6.3 Parapet patches. For a parapet the data file gives the NET coefficient GCpn, which acts on the parapet's projected
area and already accounts for both faces: +1.5 on a windward parapet and -1.0 on a leeward parapet, interpolated on
the cosine of the incidence for an oblique wind. The net parapet pressure is p = q_p * GCpn with q_p the velocity
pressure at the top of that parapet, not at mean roof height - the screen wall on the north elevation reaches well
above the deck and its velocity pressure is correspondingly higher.
6.4 Internal pressure is not part of this study.
7. Data file
WT-2026-07_Cp_by_azimuth.csv, columns patch_id, azimuth_deg, cp. One row per patch per azimuth.
8. Uncertainty

--- Page 2 ---
WT-2026-07 Boundary Layer Wind Study
page 2
The tap-to-tap repeatability of the reported means is +/- 0.03 in Cp. The coefficients are reported to four decimal places
for traceability, not because they are known to that precision.
9. Limitations
The study covers the as-built massing of 2026. It does not cover the roof-mounted equipment, the screen wall's own
component-and-cladding pressures, or any future Building A3 to the east.
